# Independent root audit: the all-dimensional rational lower bound


I read the complete proof and checked its polynomial and sign arguments.
The exact symbolic verifier also passes all arbitrary-d identities.

With x=1+z, the three rational identities have the correct powers
and denominator factors. Q has strictly positive coefficients for
every integer d>=2. The difference is exactly xP divided by a
positive denominator on x>=0. In particular the separate factor x
accounts for equality at z=-1; it is not a missing positive root.

The first four derivative values at z0 agree. Multiplication by the
denominator and division by x, both analytic and nonzero at x1,
therefore give a root of P at1 of multiplicity at least4. For j<d,
the first positive term defining P contributes no coefficient.
The resulting normalized coefficient sequence starts positive and
strictly decreases, because both displayed index fractions increase
(the first strictly). Hence it has at most one sign change after
zero coefficients are omitted. Only three coefficient positions
remain. The full polynomial has at most four sign changes.

Descartes' rule counts roots with multiplicity. Since P is nonzero
and already has a positive root of multiplicity at least4, that
root has multiplicity exactly4 and no other positive root exists.
P(0)>0 determines its sign on(0,1), and the even multiplicity
preserves the positive sign on(1,infinity). This proves the global
pointwise bound, rather than merely a bound on a finite interval.
The leading-coefficient check is consistent but unnecessary.

Pairing at v and-v is legitimate for0<=v<=1. The exact remainder
uses c=e+1/2 and thus c^2=e+e^2+1/4. Both quadratic denominators
are positive; their product D is at most1 because
D-1=v^2[(e-1/4)-e^2(1-v^2)]<=0. Consequently the remainder is at
least(theta/4)v^4, strictly positive for v>0. The endpoint v1
has no zero denominator. At v0 the integral expression has the
stated limit by the checked second derivative.

The proof is uniform in all integer d>=2 and does not rest on
fixed-dimensional checks. The supplemental checker verifies the
symbolic identities for arbitrary d and audits coefficientresearch-agent
formulas through d40. The resulting integral gap is at least
v^2/[4(d+1)], useful for the separate uniform discrete-limit audit.
No mixed-integer center or general OC conclusion is asserted here.
